event: US: Nasdaq (NASD Automated Quotations) begins operating on 8 February 1971 as an electronic quotation system; it displays prices but does not execute trades.
source: Chase. "The History of Nasdaq." JPMorgan Chase, n.d. https://www.chase.com/personal/investments/learning-and-insights/article/history-of-nasdaq.

event: US: NYSE Designated Order Turnaround (DOT) starts 1 March 1976, routing small orders electronically to the specialist; built by SIAC after a 1972 SEC rule proposal; renamed SuperDot in 1984.
source: Securities and Exchange Commission Historical Society. "Automating the Exchanges 1976-1995: NYSE." Transformation & Regulation: Equities Market Structure, 1934 to 2018. https://sechistorical.org/exhibition/transformation-regulation-equities-market-structure-1934-to-2018-2/automating-the-exchanges-1976-1995/nyse/.

event: US: 19 October 1987 crash; program trading (automated basket orders) is examined by the Brady Commission, CFTC and SEC, which disagree on its role and on how to measure it.
source: US General Accounting Office. "Testimony T-GGD-88-33: Preliminary Observations on the October 1987 Crash." 1988. https://www.gao.gov/assets/t-ggd-88-33.pdf.

event: US: GAO reviews 10 NYSE member firms' basket-trading systems: NYSE systems cannot tell trading strategies apart; 6 of 10 firms' systems can identify program trading, the other 4 see no need because NYSE does not require it.
structure: Firm systems that identify program-trading orders (voluntary)
source: US General Accounting Office. "Financial Markets: Capability of Automated Systems To Identify Program Trading (IMTEC-88-36)." April 1988. https://www.gao.gov/products/imtec-88-36.

event: US: Market-wide circuit breakers introduced in 1988 on the Brady Commission's recommendation (the NYSE had none before the crash); later codified as Rule 80B.
structure: Market-wide trading halts (venue-level automatic check)
source: Brady, Nicholas F., and Robert R. Glauber. "Circuit Breakers Are Doing Their Job, but Don't Close the Markets." NYSE. https://www.nyse.com/article/circuit-breakers-are-doing-their-job-but-dont-close-the-markets.

event: US: SEC Automation Review Policy I (16 November 1989) asks SROs to set up voluntary capacity-planning and vulnerability-assessment programmes for their automated trading systems; ARP II (9 May 1991) specifies reviews and reports to the SEC.
structure: SRO capacity and vulnerability assessment programmes with reports to SEC
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Policy Statement: Automated Systems of Self-Regulatory Organizations." Release No. 34-27445, 16 November 1989. https://www.sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/arp-i.

event: UK: London Stock Exchange launches SETS electronic order book (20 October 1997), automatically matching orders in FTSE 100 shares.
source: Euromoney. "London Stock Exchange: The Big Fizzle?" Euromoney. https://www.euromoney.com/article/b1320crvsnrmc5/london-stock-exchange-the-big-fizzle.

event: US: NASD Rule 3013 (compliance date 1 December 2004): each member designates a chief compliance officer and the CEO certifies annually that compliance processes exist, after meeting the CCO; report goes to board and audit committee. Later reused for market-access certification.
structure: Chief compliance officer; annual CEO certification of compliance processes
source: Willkie Farr & Gallagher. "New NASD Rule 3013 Requires Designation of Chief Compliance Officer." November 2004. https://www.willkie.com/publications/2004/11/new-nasd-rule-3013-requires-designation-of-chief__.

event: US: Regulation NMS Order Protection Rule: trading centres must keep policies preventing trade-throughs of quotations that are immediately and automatically accessible; widely cited as driving fragmentation and high-frequency trading.
structure: Trading-centre policies and procedures against trade-throughs
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Regulation NMS; Final Rule." Federal Register 70 (29 June 2005): 37496. https://www.govinfo.gov/link/fr/70/37559.

event: UK: Lloyd's launches a fidelity policy covering banks' losses from concealed or falsely recorded trades by rogue (human) traders. No algorithm-specific trading-error cover found in searches.
source: Risk.net. "Lloyd's Offers Insurance against Rogue Trading." 2008. https://risk.net/risk-management/1507096/lloyds-offers-insurance-against-rogue-trading.

event: US: CME advisory: orders from an automated trading system must carry a Tag 50 operator ID unique to the person, or identified team on the same shift, responsible for operating it; clearing members keep registration accurate.
structure: Registered operator ID per automated trading system (named responsible operator)
source: CME Group. "Identification and Registration of Globex Operator IDs (Tag 50 IDs)." Market Regulation Advisory RA0908-5, 2009. https://www.cmegroup.com/rulebook/files/CME_Group_RA0908-5.pdf.

event: US: a handful of high-frequency trading firms account for an estimated 70% of US equity volume in 2009; NYSE average daily volume is up 164% on 2005.
source: Clark, Carol. "Controlling Risk in a Lightning-Speed Trading Environment." Chicago Fed Letter no. 272, March 2010. https://www.chicagofed.org/publications/chicago-fed-letter/2010/march-272.

event: US: NYSE decommissions the Daily Program Trading Report, through which member organizations had reported program trading activity, replacing it with audit-trail data.
structure: Daily Program Trading Report (member reporting of program trades)
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness, SR-NYSE-2009-60." Release No. 34-60179, 2009. https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nyse/2009/34-60179.pdf.

event: FIA Market Access Working Group (clearing firms, trading firms, exchanges) issues Market Access Risk Management Recommendations (April 2010): pre-trade order checks, post-trade checks, conformance testing and error-trade policies.
structure: Pre-trade order checks and conformance testing
source: FIA. "FIA Issues Direct Market Access Recommendations." April 2010. https://www.fia.org/fia/articles/fia-issues-direct-market-access-recommendations.

event: US: 6 May 2010 Flash Crash; market-wide circuit breakers do not trigger. SEC and exchanges start a single-stock circuit breaker pilot (pause on a 10% move in five minutes).
structure: Single-stock circuit breakers
source: Seyfarth Shaw. "Recommendations of the Joint CFTC-SEC Advisory Committee on Emerging Regulatory Issues Regarding Responses to the May 6, 2010 Flash Crash." 2011. https://www.seyfarth.com/news-insights/recommendations-of-the-joint-cftc-sec-advisory-committee-on-emerging-regulatory-issues-regarding-responses-to-the-may-6-2010-flash-crash.html.

event: US: SEC adopts Rule 15c3-5 (3 November 2010; compliance 2011): bans naked access; broker-dealers must run pre-trade credit, capital and erroneous-order controls under their direct and exclusive control, reviewed at least annually under written procedures.
structure: Pre-trade market-access risk controls under broker's direct and exclusive control; documented annual review
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Risk Management Controls for Brokers or Dealers with Market Access." Federal Register, 15 November 2010. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2010/11/15/2010-28303/risk-management-controls-for-brokers-or-dealers-with-market-access.

event: US: Rule 15c3-5 requires the CEO (or equivalent) to certify annually that market-access risk controls and supervisory procedures comply and that the annual review was done; separate from the FINRA 3130 certification.
structure: Annual CEO certification of market-access controls
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Small Entity Compliance Guide: Risk Management Controls for Brokers or Dealers with Market Access." 2010. https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/final/2010/34-63241-secg.htm.

event: EU: ESMA Guidelines on systems and controls in an automated trading environment take effect 1 May 2012: firms must employ enough staff with the skills to manage electronic trading systems; cover algorithms, DMA and sponsored access.
structure: Skilled staff to manage electronic trading systems
source: Autoriteit Financiële Markten. "ESMA Guidelines Automated Trading." 2015. https://www.afm.nl/~/profmedia/files/rapporten/engels/esma-guidelines-automated-trading.ashx.

event: US: Knight Capital (1 August 2012) loses about $440 million in 45 minutes after new code reaches seven of eight SMARS servers; accounts drawing on the SEC order report no second-engineer review and no written deployment procedures.
source: Knight Capital Group. "Form 10-Q for the Quarter Ended June 30, 2012." SEC EDGAR, 2012. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060749/000119312512346917/d361681d10q.htm.

event: Germany: High-Frequency Trading Act (May 2013): BaFin licence for HFT firms; from 1 April 2014 every order from a trading algorithm must carry a unique algorithm identifier; supervisors may demand information on and prohibit strategies.
structure: Algorithm flagging (unique ID per algorithm) and HFT licence
source: Morgan Lewis. "Germany Enacts High-Frequency Trading Act." 8 March 2013. https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/im_lf_germanenactshigh-frequencytradingact_08mar13.

event: US: SEC fines Knight Capital $12 million (16 October 2013), its first market access rule case: no control comparing orders leaving the router with those entering it, and no adequate review of control effectiveness.
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "SEC Charges Knight Capital with Violations of Market Access Rule." Press Release 2013-222, 16 October 2013. https://www.sec.gov/news/press-release/2013-222.

event: EU: MiFID II Article 17 (adopted 2014; applied 3 January 2018 after a one-year delay): firms engaged in algorithmic trading must notify their home regulator and each venue; the regulator may demand strategy descriptions, trading limits, compliance and risk controls and test records.
structure: Algorithmic-trading notification to regulator and venues
source: European Securities and Markets Authority. "Article 17 Algorithmic Trading." Interactive Single Rulebook, MiFID II. https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-and-data/interactive-single-rulebook/mifid-ii/article-17-algorithmic-trading.

event: US: Nasdaq files an optional kill switch for members (2014): members set net notional exposure and volatility thresholds and can halt trading instantly; Citadel argues voluntary exchange-by-exchange kill switches are not enough after Knight.
structure: Exchange-offered kill switch
source: Compliance Week. "Nasdaq Will Use Kill Switches to Halt Trades, Prevent Flash Crashes." 2014. https://complianceweek.com/nasdaq-will-use-kill-switches-to-halt-trades-prevent-flash-crashes/14117.article.

event: US: SEC adopts Regulation SCI (19 November 2014), replacing the voluntary Automation Review Policy: exchanges, large ATSs and clearing agencies need system policies, corrective action, SEC notification and annual systems reviews; broker-dealers excluded.
structure: Annual SCI systems review and incident notification
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity." Federal Register, 5 December 2014. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2014/12/05/2014-27767/regulation-systems-compliance-and-integrity.

event: US: FINRA Regulatory Notice 15-09 (March 2015) sets supervision and control practices for algorithmic strategies across risk assessment, code development and implementation, testing and validation, trading systems and compliance, covering the whole development lifecycle.
structure: Supervision of algorithm development lifecycle (developers, testing, compliance)
source: FINRA. "Regulatory Notice 15-09: Effective Supervision and Control Practices for Firms Engaging in Algorithmic Trading Strategies." March 2015. https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/15-09.

event: US: SEC fines Goldman Sachs $7 million (30 June 2015) for 16,000 mispriced options orders on 20 August 2013: unreasonably wide pre-market price checks, and an employee lifted electronic circuit-breaker blocks on outgoing messages.
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "SEC Charges Goldman Sachs with Violating Market Access Rule." Press Release 2015-133, 30 June 2015. https://www.sec.gov/news/press-release/2015-133.

event: US: CFTC proposes Regulation AT (17 December 2015; supplement 2016): registration of some direct-access algorithmic traders and source-code repositories for registrants. Withdrawn effective 15 July 2020: no new registration and no source-code access without subpoena.
structure: Proposed registration of algorithmic traders; source-code repository
source: Commodity Futures Trading Commission. "Withdrawal of Regulation Automated Trading." Federal Register 2020-14383, 2020. https://www.cftc.gov/LawRegulation/FederalRegister/final-rules/2020-14383.html.

event: EU/UK: AFME and the Investment Association publish standardised questionnaires (24 March 2016) for buy-side firms to obtain information from brokers on how their algorithms work; updated for MiFID II in November 2017.
structure: Buy-side due-diligence questionnaire on broker algorithms
source: AFME. "Investors and Brokers Unite to Make Algo Trading More Transparent." Press release, 24 March 2016. https://www.afme.eu/globalassets/downloads/press-releases/2016/20160324_press-release_investors-and-brokers-unite-to-make-algo-trading-more-transparent-31.pdf.

event: UK: FCA adds an algorithmic trading certification function to the Senior Managers and Certification Regime for banks, building societies and PRA-designated firms; staff identified by 7 September 2016 and certified fit and proper by 7 March 2017.
structure: Algorithmic trading certification function
source: Financial Conduct Authority. "FCA Confirms Accountability Rules for Wholesale Traders and Interim Rules on Regulatory References." Press release, 2016. https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/fca-confirms-accountability-rules-wholesale-traders-and-interim-rules-regulatory.

event: US: FINRA Regulatory Notice 16-21: from 30 January 2017 anyone primarily responsible for design, development or significant modification of an equity algorithmic strategy, or supervising it day to day, must pass Series 57 and register as a Securities Trader; a registered principal supervises them under Rule 3110.
structure: Registered algorithm developer (Securities Trader) plus designated supervising principal
source: FINRA. "Regulatory Notice 16-21: Registration of Associated Persons Who Develop Algorithmic Trading Strategies." June 2016. https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/16-21.

event: EU: Market Abuse Regulation Article 16 and Delegated Regulation 2016/957 (apply 3 July 2016): firms executing orders need surveillance systems producing alerts on preset parameters with human analysis by trained staff, and must file suspicious transaction and order reports.
structure: Order and trade surveillance system with trained analysts; STOR reporting
source: European Commission. "Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/957." 9 March 2016. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2016/957/data.html.

event: US: FINRA sends member firms its first monthly cross-market equities supervision report cards on spoofing and layering (April 2016), as a preventive compliance tool.
structure: FINRA cross-market report cards to firms
source: FINRA. "FINRA Issues First Cross-Market Report Cards Covering Spoofing and Layering." News release, 2016. https://finra.org/media-center/news-releases/2016/finra-issues-first-cross-market-report-cards-covering-spoofing-and.

event: US: SEC fines Merrill Lynch $12.5 million (September 2016) because its market-access limits were set too high (5 million shares for a stock trading 79,000 a day) and its CEO certifications were deficient in 2013-14; exchanges add $3 million.
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "Merrill Lynch Charged with Trading Controls Failures That Led to Mini-Flash Crashes." Press Release 2016-192, September 2016. https://www.sec.gov/news/press-release/2016-192.

event: US: SEC charges a broker-dealer CEO (Wilson-Davis) for the first time for signing the market-access certification without knowing who was responsible for compliance or asking about the annual review.
structure: Annual CEO certification of market-access controls
source: US Securities and Exchange Commission. "SEC Settles Charges against Broker-Dealer Personnel for Violating Market Structure Rules." Press Release 2016-266, December 2016. https://www.sec.gov/news/pressrelease/2016-266.html.

event: EU/UK: RTS 6 (Delegated Regulation 2017/589) applies from 3 January 2018: a formalised governance arrangement with clear accountability lines, including approval of algorithm deployment and updates, and separation of trading desks from risk and compliance.
structure: Governance arrangement approving algorithm deployment and updates
source: European Commission. "Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/589, Chapter I." legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2017/589/chapter/I/data.htm.

event: EU/UK: RTS 6 Article 2: compliance staff must have at least a general understanding of the algorithms and continuous contact with technical staff. Article 12: kill functionality to cancel any or all unexecuted orders immediately; Article 16: real-time monitoring.
structure: Compliance staff contact with technical staff; kill functionality; real-time monitoring
source: European Commission. "Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/589, Article 2." legislation.gov.uk. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2017/589/article/2.

event: EU/UK: RTS 6 Article 9: annual self-assessment and validation of algorithmic systems, governance, continuity and compliance; the risk management function draws up the validation report (in practice reviewed by business control, operational risk or compliance).
structure: Annual self-assessment and validation report
source: Deloitte UK. "MiFID II RTS 6 Requirements: Annual Self-Assessment." Blog. https://www.deloitte.com/uk/en/services/audit-assurance/blogs/mifid-ii-rts-6-requirements-annual-self-assessment.html.

event: UK: FCA report Algorithmic Trading Compliance in Wholesale Markets (12 February 2018): firms need a process to identify algorithmic trading, define material changes and keep a full inventory of algorithms; covers development, testing, risk controls, governance and conduct.
structure: Algorithm inventory and material-change definition
source: Financial Conduct Authority. "Algorithmic Trading Compliance in Wholesale Markets." February 2018. https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/multi-firm-reviews/algorithmic-trading-compliance-wholesale-markets.pdf.

event: UK: PRA SS5/18 (effective 30 June 2018): the board, or its risk committee, approves the algorithmic trading governance framework, and the management body names the Senior Management Function(s) responsible for algorithmic trading.
structure: Board or risk-committee approval of algo governance; named SMF for algorithmic trading
source: Prudential Regulation Authority. "PS12/18: Algorithmic Trading." Bank of England, June 2018. https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/policy-statement/2018/ps1218.

event: UK: PRA SS5/18: governance framework assigns owners for the algo trading policy, algorithm approval, inventories, kill-switch controls and incident review; approval requires risk controls in place first, and each function (front office, risk) signs off its own risks. Manual and automated kill switches; restart needs manual intervention by named authorised staff.
structure: Multi-function algorithm approval process; kill-switch and inventory owners; incident review
source: Prudential Regulation Authority. "SS5/18 Algorithmic Trading." Bank of England, June 2018. https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2018/ss518.pdf.

event: UK: SM&CR extends to all FCA solo-regulated firms (9 December 2019); the algorithmic trading certification function, described as covering people who approve deployment of a trading algorithm, applies to UK-based staff.
structure: Algorithmic trading certification function
source: Katten Muchin Rosenman. "The Senior Managers & Certification Regime: One Year to Go before SMCR Applies to All FCA-Regulated Firms." 2018. https://katten.com/One-Year-to-Go-Before-SMCR-Applies-to-All-FCA-Regulated-Firms.

event: US: CFTC adopts Electronic Trading Risk Principles (8 December 2020) for designated contract markets: rules for participants, exchange-based pre-trade risk controls on all electronic orders, prompt notice of significant disruptions.
structure: Exchange-based pre-trade risk controls; disruption notification
source: Commodity Futures Trading Commission. "Electronic Trading Risk Principles." Federal Register 2020-27622, December 2020. https://www.cftc.gov/LawRegulation/FederalRegister/finalrules/2020-27622.html.

event: US: Citi advertises a Head of E-Trading Risk & Control in New York (2021), leading a first-line team in the Markets COO function that monitors algorithmic trading in real time for disorderly trading. First appearance of the title not established.
structure: Head of E-Trading Risk & Control (first-line real-time monitoring team)
source: ACCA Careers. "MSS NAM Head of E-Trading Risk & Control" (Citi job posting). 2021. https://jobs.accaglobal.com/job/8273338/mss-nam-head-of-e-trading-risk-and-control/.

event: Ireland (EU): Central Bank thematic review (May 2021) of RTS 6 compliance finds minimal board involvement in setting or challenging key controls and in overseeing algorithm development, little board reporting and no formal governance documents.
structure: Board oversight of algorithmic trading controls (found weak)
source: Central Bank of Ireland. "Central Bank Publishes Review of Firms Undertaking Algorithmic Trading." Press release, 11 May 2021. https://www.centralbank.ie/news/article/press-release-review-of-firms-undertaking-algorithmic-trading-11-May-2021.

event: EU: ESMA and national regulators launch a Common Supervisory Action (January 2024) on pre-trade controls at algorithmic trading firms, covering calibration, hard and soft blocks, governance and outsourcing, after the May 2022 flash crash.
structure: Pre-trade controls with hard and soft blocks
source: European Securities and Markets Authority. "ESMA and NCAs to Coordinate Supervisory Activities on MiFID II Pre-Trade Controls." January 2024. https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/esma-and-ncas-coordinate-supervisory-activities-mifid-ii-pre-trade-controls.

event: UK: PRA (£33.9m) and FCA (£27.8m) fine Citigroup Global Markets (22 May 2024) for the 2 May 2022 error, when a $58m basket became $444bn, $189bn reached a trading algorithm and $1.4bn of European equities sold: no hard block to stop the whole basket, an overridable pop-up warning, and real-time monitoring too slow to escalate alerts.
structure: Hard blocks; real-time monitoring escalation
source: Financial Reporter. "FCA and PRA Fine Citigroup £61m." May 2024. https://financialreporter.co.uk/fca-and-pra-fine-citigroup-61m.html.

event: FIA publishes Best Practices for Automated Trading Risk Controls and System Safeguards (18 July 2024): pre-trade limits, kill switches, cancel-on-disconnect, drop-copy reconciliation; said to fit AI-driven trading too.
structure: Pre-trade limits, kill switches and post-trade reconciliation
source: FIA. "FIA Releases Best Practices for Automated Trading Risk Controls and System Safeguards." 18 July 2024. https://www.fia.org/fia/articles/fia-releases-best-practices-automated-trading-risk-controls-and-system-safeguards.

event: US: SEC withdraws 14 proposals (12 June 2025), among them the 2023 plan to extend Regulation SCI to larger broker-dealers and the predictive data analytics rule.
source: Sullivan & Cromwell, via CLS Blue Sky Blog. "Sullivan & Cromwell Discusses SEC Withdrawal of 14 Proposed Rules." 23 June 2025. https://clsbluesky.law.columbia.edu/2025/06/23/sullivan-cromwell-discusses-sec-withdrawal-of-14-proposed-rules/.

event: UK: FCA consults on SM&CR reform (CP25/21, 15 July 2025): cut certification roles by about 15% and possibly replace the Certification Regime later; a 2023 FIA/EPTA letter had named the algorithmic trading function as one to remove.
structure: Algorithmic trading certification function (under review)
source: Mayer Brown. "FAQs on Proposed Reforms to the UK Senior Managers and Certification Regime." 23 July 2025. https://www.mayerbrown.com/en/insights/publications/2025/07/faqs-on-proposed-reforms-to-the-uk-senior-managers-and-certification-regime.

event: UK: FCA multi-firm review of principal trading firms (August 2025): self-assessments better than 2018, but some compliance teams lack technical knowledge, inventories omit who is approved to operate each algorithm, material change is undefined and boards get too little information on deployments.
structure: Algorithm inventory with approved operator; board MI on deployments
source: Financial Conduct Authority. "Multi-Firm Review of Algorithmic Trading Controls: High-Level Observations." August 2025. https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/multi-firm-reviews/algorithmic-trading-controls-high-level-observations.

event: EU: ESMA supervisory briefing on algorithmic trading (26 February 2026): convergence on governance, testing, outsourcing and pre-trade controls (incl. market-making quotes); firms should consider AI's influence in annual self-assessments.
structure: Annual self-assessment extended to AI influence
source: CMS. "ESMA Supervisory Briefing on Algorithmic Trading in the EU: Key Points and Practical Implications." 2026. https://cms.law/en/gbr/legal-updates/esma-supervisory-briefing-on-algorithmic-trading-in-the-eu-key-points-and-practical-implications.

event: Netherlands (EU): AFM (1 April 2026) folds the ESMA briefing into supervision, expects explainable, auditable algorithms with clear lines of accountability, and will request RTS 6 validation reports from firms and banks in Q3 2026.
structure: RTS 6 validation report requested by supervisor
source: Autoriteit Financiële Markten. "Supervision of Algorithmic Trading Tightened." 1 April 2026. https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/actueel/2026/apr/sb-algohandel-aangescherpt.

event: US: Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC issue SR 26-2 (17 April 2026), revised model risk guidance replacing SR 11-7 (April 2011, which required independent model validation), most relevant to banks over $30 billion; commentators note a narrower model definition and validation timed by materiality.
structure: Model risk management and validation (revised)
source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. "SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management." 17 April 2026. https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/sr2602.htm.

event: FIX Trading Community publishes Recommended Practices for Algorithm Testing and Certification (reported June 2026): standard messages to test, certify and approve algorithms for production, and share certificates with counterparties and regulators.
structure: Algorithm certification certificate shared with counterparties
source: Mondo Visione. "FIX Releases New Guidelines on Algo Testing and Certification." 2026. https://mondovisione.com/media-and-resources/news/fix-releases-new-guidelines-on-algo-testing-and-certification-202663/.

event: US/UK: Citi advertises a Global Head of E-Trading Risk Management (London and New York, September 2026), leading second-line oversight of electronic and algorithmic trading and setting the e-trading risk framework.
structure: Global Head of E-Trading Risk Management (second line)
source: Citi Careers. "Global Head of E-Trading Risk Management." Job posting, 2026. https://jobs.citi.com/job/london/global-head-of-e-trading-risk-management/287/100308149872.
